subject: Finova SLOs: regional routing & multi-region performance follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir@finova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Finova SLOs: regional routing & multi-region performance follow-up

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the performance & routing requirements: 

Summary of asks from the call:
- Latency targets: 95th percentile end-to-end <= 150ms for US customers, <= 200ms for EU, <= 250ms for APAC (user-facing inference).
- Throughput: baseline 2k tokens/s sustained per region, burst capacity to 8k tokens/s for 30s windows.
- Concurrency: average UI concurrency ~200 concurrent requests, peak ~800 requests.
- Streaming: client requires token-streaming for chat UX (low-latency token-by-token delivery); must support server-sent events or chunked HTTP.
- Regional routing & data residency: EU traffic must stay within EU, APAC traffic should route to APAC region; US can use multi-AZ in us-west/us-east. EU data (including logs and request metadata) must be stored in EU for EU tenants.

Questions / confirmations we need from your side:
1) Can you confirm which Finova product segments must have EU-only residency vs. global? (we heard payments & PII-heavy flows need EU-only)
2) Expected average request size (tokens) and distribution across regions for next 6 months — helps us size Dedicated pools.
3) Any regulatory constraints around streaming payloads (e.g., cannot include full utterance in logs)?

Next steps I propose:
- We'll share an SLO matrix (attached) mapping latency/throughput to recommended Dedicated sizing and routing policies.
- Aditya will validate streaming support and provide a short ops runbook for achieving <150ms p95 in US.
- If the numbers look good, we can schedule a tech deep-dive (30-45m) next week to finalize capacity and timing.

Attaching: SLO_matrix_Finova_v1.xlsx and redwood_arch_diagram.pdf (high-level).

Thanks — looking forward to the answers to the three questions so we can size the proposal.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Samir Desai <samir@finova.com>

Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova SLOs: regional routing & multi-region performance follow-up

Thanks Marissa — appreciated the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Residency: Payments and Customer Profile services must be EU-only for EU customers. Other services (e.g., marketing workflows) can be global. We’ll provide a scoped list by Tuesday.
2) Token sizes: average request ~120 tokens; chat history average 6 messages (~650 tokens) for long-tail flows. Region distribution today: US 62%, EU 30%, APAC 8%; expect EU to grow to ~38% in 6 months as we expand.
3) Streaming logs: Security team asks that full utterance not be stored in logs for EU customers; metadata and token timing ok.

We’re keen to see the SLO matrix. Tech deep-dive next Wed (28th) between 9-11am PT works for our engineering manager.

Samir
Head of Product, Finova
samir@finova.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova SLOs: regional routing & multi-region performance follow-up

Hi Samir — quick technical notes based on Marissa’s recap and your clarifications: 

- Streaming: Redwood supports chunked HTTP streaming and server-sent events today; we can guarantee sub-50ms inter-token latency from our runtime once the request is routed to a local pool. We will add the log-redaction option for EU tenants so full utterances are not persisted.

- Latency targets: achieving p95 <=150ms in US for the worst-case (650 token context) requires:
  * Dedicated GPU pool in US-west with 2x capacity headroom for burst (we recommend A100 or equivalent).
  * Prefix caching for common prompts and KV cache warm-up to save ~20-40ms on long-context calls.

- Throughput/concurrency: to meet baseline 2k tokens/s sustained with 800 concurrent requests peak we estimate needing ~6 concurrently active GPUs (model/quantization dependent). For the projected EU growth we recommend reserve capacity in EU-central (Frankfurt) with autoscale up to 4 GPUs.

- Regional routing & residency: we can configure request routing by tenant region and enforce data residency on storage/logging. For EU-only tenants we’ll pin models and logging to the EU control plane; cross-region fallbacks can be disabled per-tenant.

I'll prepare a short ops runbook (20-30m read) with sizing assumptions and validation steps ahead of the Wed deep-dive. Can you confirm the Wed 28th 9:30am PT slot?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
